topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory welcome and frames the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate recognition of pathogens, cellular damage, and pattern recognition receptor pathways
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns and their corresponding receptor and inflammasome signaling pathways.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammatory consequences
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the cellular cascade of acute inflammation, including sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment into tissue, lymphatic drainage, and systemic complications such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: They address how acute inflammation is brought to an end, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how the body adapts to persistent stimuli through chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on complement.
